item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the requested, narrowly scoped upload fix. It implements replayable buffered uploads and the required tests without A’s broad retry and body-ownership refactor, though B still violates important contract details.","reasons":["B directly tests multipart field/name/content, retrying content read from an *os.File, validation before requests, and source-reader error propagation. A lacks a visible Upload source-reader-error test and tests Upload retry with strings.Reader rather than the reported streamed source.","B leaves Files.Add and the shared RawClient machinery unchanged. A changes retry behavior, Content-Length handling, empty-body handling, and caller-body closing semantics across Raw.Do, explicitly exceeding the contract’s scope.","Both patches improperly duplicate Files.Add request/response logic by calling Raw.Do directly instead of routing Upload through Add.","Both add association options despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior. B’s added surface is smaller; A additionally adds project association, arbitrary form values, validation machinery, and a generalized multipart-fields implementation."],"risks_a":["The global adoptRequestBody change alters semantics for Files.Update, Persons.AddPicture, Raw.Do, and all seekable request bodies, contrary to the frozen scope.","Its GetBody closure reuses and seeks the same caller-owned reader instead of producing an independent body, making the general abstraction fragile outside strictly sequential retries.","It changes ownership by preventing transport closure of caller-supplied io.Closers and converts empty seekable bodies to http.NoBody; neither behavior was requested under the frozen contract for Add or Raw.Do."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating its request construction, decoding, missing-data check, and error path.","The new WithFile*ID options violate the exact API/scope contract, perform no ID validation, and have misleading comments saying they apply to Add even though Add ignores cfg.form.","The helper extension and association-field tests are unnecessary machinery for the contracted single-file multipart upload."]}
